security_spec.violation_condition: In the mip CSR hardware module, if STIP read-only behavior is gated on the elaboration-time presence of stimecmp hardware (e.g., a Chisel 'if (hasSstc)' guarding writability) rather than on the runtime menvcfg.STCE bit. Specifically, when menvcfg.STCE=0—meaning the Sstc extension is disabled by M-mode firmware—the hardware must allow M-mode software to write mip.STIP to inject timer interrupts to S-mode. If the implementation instead treats STIP as permanently read-only whenever stimecmp registers exist in the RTL, writes to mip.STIP are silently dropped when STCE=0.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mip.STIP writability gated on compile-time/elaboration-time stimecmp presence (e.g., conditional 'when' block keyed on HasSstc parameter) rather than on runtime menvcfg.STCE via Mux(menvcfg.STCE.asBool, platformIRP.STIP, reg.STIP)
security_spec.summary: STIP read-only in mip must depend on runtime menvcfg.STCE=1, not on hardware-implemented stimecmp alone; STCE=0 requires software-writable STIP even with stimecmp present

findings.finding: mip.STIP writability is correctly gated on the runtime menvcfg.STCE bit, not on a compile-time parameter. When menvcfg.STCE=0 (Sstc disabled), M-mode writes to mip.STIP are accepted via the register path; when menvcfg.STCE=1 (Sstc enabled), STIP is read-only and reflects platformIRP.STIP from the SstcInterruptGen hardware. This correctly implements the spec requirement that STIP reverts to writable behavior when STCE=0.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

If the stimecmp register is not implemented, STIP is writable in mip, and may be written by M-mode software to deliver timer interrupts to S-mode. If the stimecmp (supervisor-mode timer compare) register is implemented, STIP is read-only in mip and reflects the supervisor-level timer interrupt signal resulting from stimecmp.

findings.finding: The menvcfg.STCE field RW-ness is correctly controlled by the compile-time CSRConfig.EXT_SSTC parameter: when Sstc is implemented, STCE is RW (reset=1); when Sstc is not implemented, STCE defaults to RO (reset=0) from the EnvCfg base class. The compile-time parameter only controls whether the field itself is writable, not the downstream STIP behavior.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Sstc extension adds the STCE (STimecmp Enable) bit to menvcfg CSR. When the Sstc extension is not implemented, STCE is read-only zero.

findings.finding: The SstcInterruptGen correctly guards the STIP output with runtime menvcfg.STCE: the timer comparison is only registered when menvcfg.STCE is true. When STCE=0, the platformIRP.STIP signal stays false, which is correct since the mip module reads from reg.STIP (the software-writable register) in that case.

spec_citations.excerpt: A supervisor timer interrupt becomes pending, as reflected in the STIP bit in the mip and sip registers whenever time contains a value greater than or equal to stimecmp, treating the values as unsigned integers.

findings.finding: henvcfg.STCE is correctly forced to 0 when menvcfg.STCE=0, implementing the spec requirement that henvcfg.STCE is read-only zero when the parent menvcfg.STCE is zero.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, [...] STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero.

findings.finding: The mvip.STIP alias correctly follows the mip.STIP writability: when menvcfg.STCE=1, mvip.STIP is read-only zero; when menvcfg.STCE=0, mvip.STIP is an alias of mip.STIP and writes are forwarded to mip via toMip.STIP.valid gated on !this.menvcfg.STCE.
